Definition: a yoke (as imposed on the neck), literally or figuratively
BiblicalUsage: Ol is a yoke, laid on the neck, literally or figuratively. Isaac tells Esau in Genesis 27:40 that he will break his brother's yoke from off his neck, and the Lord says in Leviticus 26:13 that He has broken the bands of Israel's yoke. The red heifer of Numbers 19:2 must be one upon which never came yoke, and the heifer of Deuteronomy 21:3 must never have drawn in the yoke.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the yoke is the Bible's picture of bondage, and the Lord breaks yokes before He asks for service. My position is that the heifer that never bore a yoke points to the one sacrifice that was never mastered by sin.
